A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same work, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplements. Referenced supplementary material is unavailable, limiting comparison of training details, evaluation prompts and additional analyses, particularly in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original TAR-TVG benchmark results, reward and training ablations, training curves, and thinking-length measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original grounding results and reports additional VQA experiments, reasoning-quality evaluations, controlled reward comparisons and failure analysis.

M1.justification: The TVG reward components and GRPO-SFT-GRPO training sequence are retained; renamed tags, rewards and coefficient symbols do not establish algorithm changes. Section 4.2 adds a VQA inference adaptation that generates temporal anchors before a categorical answer, whereas grounding outputs the final anchor interval.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot video question answering on MVBench and VideoMME, extending evaluation beyond temporal localization to categorical question answering. The four grounding benchmarks remain. Naming TVGBench's constituent datasets and specifying QVHighlights' single-segment subset adds documentation rather than establishing new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds TRACE to the Charades comparison, VideoChat-R1.5 and Temporal-RLT to grounding comparisons, and HawkEye to ActivityNet; Momentor disappears. New evaluations compare against Video-VER and the base Qwen2.5-VL-7B. Several results labeled TimeZero in v1 are assigned to Time-R1 comparisons in v2 without explaining the reassignment.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Qwen2.5-VL-72B judging of faithfulness and autonomy on a 1–5 scale, categorical-answer zero-shot VQA evaluation, and explicitly matched-data 3B/7B reward controls in Table 6. Table 1 also changes reported training status, including TimeChat from not fine-tuned to fine-tuned. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds reasoning-quality comparisons, matched Time-R1/soft-IoU/anchor controls, and analysis of three failure modes across 3,720 samples. v1's one-to-four-anchor sweep is absent from the supplied v2. Training-strategy and reward-component ablations, soft-IoU training curves, and thinking-length analysis are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The new reasoning ratings and failure percentages add results without introducing an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: TAR's headline grounding results remain unchanged, including 61.1 Charades-STA mIoU and 65.9 QVHighlights mIoU. v2 adds VQA scores of 66.1 on MVBench and 54.9 on VideoMME, reasoning ratings, controlled reward results and a 92.1% refinement finding. ActivityNet VTimeLLM recall values change from 51.0/27.5/11.4 to 44.0/27.8/14.3. STA-only zero-shot rows and anchor-count sweep results are no longer shown.

T1.justification: v1's explicit normalized group-reward and KL-regularized GRPO objective definitions, Equations 1–2, are omitted. v2 instead introduces an autoregressive joint-generation formulation in Equation 1. The main anchor-reward mathematics remains equivalent after notation changes, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 expands the central contribution from verifiable progressive timestamp refinement to balancing reasoning faithfulness and semantic autonomy between outcome-only and fully supervised approaches. Its abstract and conclusion additionally claim that anchors counter hallucination-related textual inertia and avoid rigid reasoning patterns. The headline grounding-performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 3.1 argues that anchors interrupt textual inertia and force renewed attention to visual evidence while preserving free-form reasoning. v2 also interprets VQA results as transfer of the refinement pattern and identifies visual ambiguity, extremely short targets and near-optimal boundary variation as failure conditions. These substantive explanations and qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: The supplied v2 omits v1's concrete filtering thresholds: reward above 6.4, at least two anchors, and first/second-anchor soft IoU above 0.5/0.7. It also omits the stated epoch schedule and LoRA rank/scaling settings, referring training configurations to an unavailable supplement. Hardware reporting changes from stage/model-specific 4/8/16 A100-40GB configurations to eight A100s for all experiments. v2 adds some dataset and generation-model details, but substantially reduces directly available reproduction information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes positioning around outcome-based versus process-supervised reasoning, prominently introducing Video-VER and presenting TAR as an intermediate paradigm. It adds discussion or citations for newer methods including TVG-R1, VideoChat-R1.5, Temporal-RLT, Chain-of-Focus and Thyme, while removing TimeZero and numerous earlier background references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around faithfulness and autonomy. The methodology is reorganized with a new intuition subsection and without the GRPO preliminary subsection. The title, authorship information, terminology and section organization also change substantially.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening grounding example with a three-paradigm schematic, redraws the framework and training diagrams, merges the two zero-shot grounding tables, and adds VQA and controlled-comparison tables plus a reasoning-quality chart. Existing plots and ablations are relocated within a redesigned single-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful VQA evidence, controlled reward comparisons and failure analysis. However, it loses directly available filtering and training specifications and the anchor-count study, while deferring crucial reasoning-scoring details to an absent supplement. The unexplained reassignment of TimeZero results to Time-R1 further limits verification. These empirical benefits and reproducibility losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
